text: The blade stays where the hand holds it, and everything else curls away in thin pale shavings. Kenaz is the cut that takes off what is not the shape, until the shape stands clear. Each pass removes, and something is left standing that was not visible before. What you are making may already be further along than the pile of shavings suggests.

The blade stays where your hand holds it, and the shavings curl away and fall. Kenaz is the cut that takes off what is not the shape. The wood loses wood, Kuky, and the form underneath comes nearer with every pass. What you see now may already be clearer than what you set out to make.

Your needles keep moving though the ball of yarn has gone thin in your hand. Nauthiz is the work continuing while the supply runs low. You count what is left, Kuky, and you measure it against the rows still unmade. What you are making may be asking for more than you currently have to give it.

The needles keep moving, though the yarn thins toward its end in your hand. Nauthiz is the work continuing while the supply runs low, and the counting that begins there. Each stitch now costs more thought than the last, and the pattern narrows to what the remainder allows. What you are making may be asking for something you have not yet admitted you need.

The finished sweater lies across your knees, the needles set aside, the loose yarn still coiled in the basket. Now only the sweater — every row you worked through the dark months holding its shape at last. Jera is the slow return of what was set in motion, season after season. Something you began before you knew its final form may now be wearable.

The sweater lies finished on the table, and the loose yarn, the dark evenings, the counted rows all fall away behind it. Jera is the slow turn from work to wearable thing. Every row was made months before the shape was clear, and none of them could be hurried. Something you began without a picture of its ending may now be whole enough to wear, Kuky.
